A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Full-Duplex-Bench-v2 work. Their main text, figures, tables and appendices are readable and complete, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of GPT-Realtime, Moshi and Freeze-Omni across four task families and two pacing conditions, including Figure 2 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains those experimental results and adds a human validation study involving 120 evaluation sessions in Section 3.3 and Table 2.

M1.justification: The examiner, staged goals, pacing logic, streaming adapters and Gemini scoring procedure remain unchanged. Orchestrator details move from v1 Appendix B into Section 2.2; the added explanations of synthetic speech and model independence do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same English Daily, Correction, Entity Tracking and Safety tasks under Fast and Slow pacing. The human study scores a subset of existing evaluation sessions without adding a dialogue domain, language or test scenario.

E2.justification: Section 3.3 introduces human ratings as a reference comparison for the automated judge. The dialogue-system comparisons retain GPT-Realtime, Moshi and Freeze-Omni throughout; expanding the table label GPT to GPT-Realtime does not introduce another model.

E3.justification: v2 adds a supplementary protocol in which human annotators independently score 120 sessions spanning the existing task families and pacing conditions. The original dialogue evaluation, 1–5 scoring scales and 15-second temporal aggregation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 adds a substantive validation analysis testing whether automated scores agree with human assessment across all five metrics. This directly examines the benchmark's scoring validity, which v1 did not test with human annotations. The existing temporal-degradation and pacing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Table 2 introduces Krippendorff's alpha and Pearson correlation estimates for agreement between the judge and human annotators. v1 contains no corresponding agreement analysis. Repeated-run counts, confidence intervals and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports alpha values of 0.5879–0.6931 and Pearson correlations of 0.5877–0.6914 across the five metrics. Figure 2, Table 1 and the original appendix results table, renumbered from Table 2 to Table 3, retain their numerical results and trends.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The scoring rubrics and output schema are retained, and the new agreement statistics do not introduce mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds the claim that human agreement validates the framework's reliability for scalable assessment. The original claims about the framework's novelty, task coverage and deterioration of model performance over time remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds the claimed acoustic-control benefit and reduced prosodic variation of synthetic examiner speech. It interprets human-agreement results, acknowledges that validation does not eliminate judge bias or drift, and adds discussion of accent/cultural bias and voice-phishing risks.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the specific Parakeet-TDT-0.6b-v2 checkpoint and states that code and data are released, replacing v1's promised future release. The streaming format and adapter implementation details were already documented in v1 Appendix B.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to earlier dialogue models and benchmarks are unchanged. Appendix A retains its related-work discussion; the citation-format corrections do not change its substance.

P1.justification: v2 swaps the semantic-goal and pacing subsections, moves orchestrator details into the main text, and adds validation and risk sections. It also makes localized wording, model-name, affiliation and acknowledgment edits while retaining most existing prose.

P2.justification: v2 adds the human-agreement table and relocates existing displays as the text reflows. Figure 2 moves between columns, Table 1 moves to page 5, and the appendix results become Table 3 on page 9. Both figures retain their original visual content.

improvement.justification: The new human study provides direct validation that v1 lacked, and the checkpoint identification improves reproducibility. These are useful gains, but the study omits annotator counts, session-selection details and rating aggregation procedures. Its moderate correlations provide limited support for the stronger claim of confirmed reliability, so the overall improvement remains modest.
